item: Melody notes are few, diatonic, and long
content: Measured on user transcriptions: the melody stays in the scale and on chord notes while the chords are chromatic.
parameters: Drunk: 100 percent diatonic notes; 72 percent chord tones; 3.27 beats for each note; range G4 to G-sharp 5 (13 semitones). Threshold: range A-flat 4 to C6. Bird on the Wing: range E4 to C5
where: Drunk; Threshold; Bird on the Wing

item: Slow melody above a fast grid
content: The melodies are slow and in four. They sit on the slow pulse while the rhythm section plays the fast tuplets. Harmony and melody are organised around the pulse. A reviewer finds the leads of one track faint and hard to remember.
parameters: Melody in 4 at 58 BPM above 11 notes per beat
where: Against the Fall of Night (title track)

content: The tenor sax is the main lead voice. Sax and bass share the lead in some pieces. A shakuhachi leads one piece. The bass opens one piece. Horn licks answer the groove.
parameters: Tenor sax on 8 of 9 tracks (2024) and 5 of 10 (2021)

item: Short interjections doubled by the drums
content: In the bridge the sax and the guitar play short interjections. Neely says they 'make for very fun fills to double on the drums'. Other tracks have horn fills and string stabs.
parameters: Sax + guitar + drums in rhythmic unison for the length of a fill
where: Against the Fall of Night (title track); Whalefall; Hot Saturn

content: Guitar leads are fast and percussive. One reviewer places De La Victoria between Cory Wong and Allan Holdsworth. Another hears fusion shredding with fine detail. On record: fast progressive guitar in the track Perihelion and a guest solo by Plini in Whalefall.
parameters: A lick in Cool 7 puts 4 equal notes in a dotted quarter (dotted sixteenths; 4 notes against 3 eighths)

content: Tenor sax (Jared Yee): restrained, with space and atmosphere; he can also play free. In his solo set he layers the sax with electronics, live sampling and phasing. A half-time section of Whalefall carries a sax melody.
parameters: 1 tenor sax; solo opening set under the name Avant George

content: Neely plays lines with two-hand tapping, some as polyrhythms. A reviewer describes phrases that shift by a sixteenth note in one hand while the other hand stays constant. A solo bass spot quotes classical themes (Holst, Elgar, Bach). Threshold has a tapped bass part, played with the index and middle fingers of the right hand.
parameters: Two-hand tapping; shift of 1 sixteenth note; 1 solo spot in each concert

content: Notes closer than about 100 ms are not heard as rhythm; they become a buzz. The tuplet lines of the band sit just at this limit.
parameters: 11 per beat at 58 BPM = 94 ms. 19 per beat at 33 BPM = 96 ms (computed). 15 per beat at 60 BPM = 66 ms (too fast). World record of single drum strokes: about 50 ms
where: Against the Fall of Night; Threshold

item: Place and making of the solos
content: Solos are features inside a short form: a drum feature after the tempo change and a guest guitar solo late in the piece (Whalefall); bass and drums trade solos (Macchina); an improvised drum intro (All These People). Live, each player has a solo spot. Neely: to write a solo out is not cheating; 'Play exciting, not excited.' For improvisation he rests on beats 1 and 2 and plays on beats 3 and 4, to force clear choices.
parameters: Whalefall: drum feature after about 1:40; guitar solo as event 9 of 11. Improvisation rule: rest 2 beats, play 2 beats
source: waterson-whalefall; larsen-perihelion; neely-covers; emr-glasgow25; neely-solos; neely-qa-grahams

item: Thing of Gold: shape of the melody
content: The melody goes up from the tonic to the third, leaps to the seventh, and goes down the scale. The third is a semitone lower on the way down. A tonic pedal could hold the full line, but the band puts a new chord under each part.
parameters: Scale degrees 1 2 3 7 6 5 4 b3 2 1: 10 notes, range of a major seventh

content: A guitar player and a keyboard player double the horn line at some moments. The other keyboards and guitars play the chords. In rehearsal the horns first play the melody; an alternative is that the horns play the pads.
parameters: Doubling is a tool against a crowded texture: 2 or 3 players become 1 line

content: Lingus: a guitar hook doubles the blues-like trumpet melody. Fuel City: violin with synth. Free Fall: flute and violin share the melody; then guitar and tenor sax take the same line. Keep It On Your Mind: the guitar has the melody and the horns harmonise it.
parameters: Pairs: trumpet + guitar; violin + synth; flute + violin; guitar + tenor sax. The pair changes when the line repeats
where: We Like It Here; Empire Central

content: Shofukan: muted horns enter after the guitar. Lingus: a slow, blues-like horn melody over a funky bass riff; short horn stabs off the beat, in unison by trumpets and saxes; a shout chorus holds the track together.
parameters: Horn stabs as a 2-bar pattern off the beat (from a teaching page). Stabs at 0:13 and 0:48

content: Lingus: Cory Henry plays fast lines with the 2 hands in unison. The solo starts with chords: he enters on beats 1 and 2 of bar 4 of the section. A teacher fits an E Dorian idea to the solo. Thing of Gold: the Moog solo of Shaun Martin uses the pentatonic scale in a fluid way.
parameters: Scales named in the sources: E Dorian; pentatonic. The Lingus solo lasts 3:55

item: Syncopated lines for the full band
content: Bad Kids to the Back has syncopated lines and harmony that moves a lot. League: the lines work because "we all know and agree on how we want the subdivisions to feel".
parameters: 108 BPM (machine): 16th notes = 7.2 notes per second (derived). Much of the guitar part was programmed in the demo for the band to interpret

content: A unison line is played by guitars, bass, and keyboards; the horns join for the last part or answer it. The usual note value is the 16th note with rests and ties off the beat. The line is a riff of 1 to 4 bars that repeats. It ends on a short hit by the full band or on a held note.
parameters: 100 to 130 BPM: 6.7 to 8.7 notes per second (estimate). Scales: minor pentatonic, blues, and Dorian with chromatic passing notes (estimate). Doubling at 1 or 2 octaves (estimate). Dean Town by Vulfpeck: a bass line in constant 16th notes, about 7.3 notes per second (estimate)
where: What About Me?; Bad Kids to the Back; Dean Town

content: Solos mix blues and pentatonic phrases with bebop lines: chromatic enclosures of chord notes, diminished and altered runs, and side-steps a semitone out of the key and back. A motif repeats and moves by one 16th note against the beat. The fastest runs are sextuplets and 32nd notes.
parameters: 10 to 13 notes per second at 100 to 130 BPM (estimate). A run lasts 1 to 2 bars and ends on a long, bent note (estimate)

content: The horns play most melodies in unison or in octaves: trumpets on top, tenor sax 1 octave lower. For harmony the 3 or 4 horns play close chords of 3 notes, chords in fourths, or clusters with a second. Flugelhorns replace trumpets in soft sections. No source of this study gives the voicings.
parameters: 2 to 4 horn parts; span of a harmonised chord 1 octave or less (estimate)

content: The bass plays a "frenzied, synthy bass line" with fast fills.
parameters: Electric bass with a synth-like tone (Sam Wilkes). Keyboards and saxophone above it

content: Complex melodies. Many solos on the band tracks.
parameters: Melodic complexity (0 to 100): Overtime 92; I'm the President 98; It's All Nothing bridge 98, chorus 64. "The Abyss": drum breaks, stabbing synths and many solos (saxophone, keyboard, bass)

content: Fast riffs and chord changes at the same time.
parameters: At 160 BPM, 16th notes are 10.7 notes per second (computed)

content: She does not use the common synth lead sounds for solos. The duo often prefers the feel of a track to jazz solos.
parameters: Guests take solos: Herbie Hancock (piano, vocoder), Kurt Rosenwinkel (guitar), Thundercat (bass)

content: On records he limits fast parts. Live he plays more and faster.
parameters: He wrote slap bass lines and then learned them: 4 months of daily practice. "I'm Tight" has slap bass syncopations

item: Lead by automation; solo in a new metre
content: Leads and bass lines come from a resonator effect. The solo is the most complex section.
parameters: Pitch by automation of Tune and Decay, not by notes. Uh Oh!: solo with melodic complexity 97 in 6/8 at 185; intro 61 in 4/4 at 123

content: Fast lines in unison between lead and bass.
parameters: Synth or saxophone lead + bass 1 or 2 octaves lower + guitar. 16th notes at 130 to 176 BPM = 8.7 to 11.7 notes per second. Length 2 to 8 bars. No source that gives the doubling of each line was found (estimate)

content: Upper limit of speed named in a thesis on virtuoso guitar technique.
parameters: 32nd notes at 125 BPM = 16.7 notes a second (computed). Three-string sweep arpeggios at 163 BPM for one minute. Examples from two other players of the same scene (Jason Richardson, Rusty Cooley)

content: Notes a second = BPM / 60 x notes in one beat. Arithmetic, for use as limits in the composition code.
parameters: At 120 BPM: sixteenths 8, quintuplets 10, sextuplets 12, septuplets 14, 32nds 16. At 140: 9.3, 11.7, 14, 16.3, 18.7. At 150: 10, 12.5, 15, 17.5, 20. Estimate of the usual range of fast lead runs: 10 to 16 notes a second

content: Lead lines mix sixteenths with quintuplets and sextuplets. Streams of tapped arpeggios run in sextuplets.
parameters: Thordendal's solo in 'Stengah': quintuplets and sextuplets over the full range. Abasi lesson figure: hammered arpeggios as a stream of sextuplets with a light palm mute, one plucked note on each beat. 'Tempting Time': an arpeggio that goes down in triplets. Guitar and drums in quintuplets ('Gestaltzerfall')

content: A fast line in unison with the other instruments is a signature of the style. It must be exact in time.
parameters: Lesson example: alternate-picked unison line from E minor pentatonic with two notes on each string. In Hamasyan the voice doubles the piano melody, the left hand doubles the bass and kick, and lines are doubled in octaves

content: Standard knowledge of the band's style, not confirmed in a source read here: the keyboard lead and a guitar play the theme in unison or in octaves, then split into parallel harmony; the second guitar and the bass hold the riff.
parameters: Estimate: unison themes of 4 to 8 bars; harmony in thirds or sixths on the repeat; fast runs in sixteenths or sextuplets at 100 to 140 BPM (6.7 to 14 notes a second)

content: Sweeps cover three octaves with one fingering that repeats in each octave. Low-register sweeps start on the seventh string.
parameters: 'Tempting Time' opening: three-octave sweep in C; picking down-down-down-up-down, then the sweep goes on; the fingering is the same in the first two octaves. 'Mind-Spun': arpeggio root on the seventh string; the lowest notes are palm-muted for clarity

content: The solo is improvised in the manner of Allan Holdsworth. A written part is inserted where the notes must follow the chords. The solo can take the accents of the riff below it.
parameters: Order: improvised start, written middle, improvised end. In the second half of the 'Stengah' solo the line marks the accents of the rhythm guitar. A MIDI breath controller shapes some solos

content: Bends are rare on extended-range guitars. Each branch of the style has its own habit of vibrato.
parameters: Abasi rarely bends on 7- and 8-string guitars; exception: harmonised bends with wide vibrato ('Tooth and Claw'). Plini ends a phrase with a whole-tone bend and vibrato. Thall players use no vibrato ('mimic robots'). Meshuggah bend the lowest string from F to F# at the end of a riff to push into the next downbeat

content: Singing phrases first, fast notes second. A short melodic shape can cross the beat.
parameters: Plini: vocal style from pentatonic and diatonic notes after Joe Satriani; a three-note shape repeated in sixteenth notes (3 against 4), not in triplets. Abasi (2014): 'the right notes' in place of many notes; double stops and major triads from blues players

content: The eight-string is used over its full range 'like a piano or harp'. Hamasyan puts riff lines in the lowest octaves of the piano.
parameters: Eight-string in drop E: E1 (41.2 Hz) to E6 at fret 24 of the first string = five octaves (computed). 'Entertain Me': lines in the two lowest octaves; one section of 'Double-Faced' needs two bass clefs

content: Not confirmed in a source read here. Lead lines alternate long notes and runs and leave short rests; the riff below fills the rests.
parameters: Estimate: 2 to 4 bars of long notes with bends, then a run of 1 to 2 bars; a rest of 1 or 2 beats before the next phrase; the fastest run comes near the end of a solo; solos of 16 to 32 bars

item: Cells and speed of the lines
content: Short cells of 3, 5, and 7 eighth notes inside the bar of 19. Fast lines for guitar, violin, and keyboard.
parameters: Solo: motifs of 5/8 and 7/8; a 3/8 cell repeated; triplets; 4 notes against the last 3/8; bends of a minor third; one chorus of 11 bars. At quarter note = 216 (computed): eighth notes = 7.2 notes per second; eighth-note triplets = 10.8 notes per second. Review: a guitar and violin figure of about 12 notes at "machine-gun speed"
where: Celestial Terrestrial Commuters; Birds of Fire

content: The bass guitar plays the melody and the bass line at once.
parameters: Sixteenth notes; intro of 4 bars (drums, synthesizer, soprano sax); a bass synthesizer doubles the line; drums recorded first, bass added after; fretless Jazz bass of 1962; 2:51

content: The bass plays a melody in artificial harmonics above a synthesizer bass riff.
parameters: Synthesizer riff: three phrases of 4 bars (12 bars; computed 18.5 s at 156 BPM). Then a bass melody of 16 bars in harmonics; the second 8 bars go up an octave. The right thumb touches the string at the octave point

content: Two unlike instruments play the theme together.
parameters: Bowed double bass in unison with the saxophone (Orange Lady, 8:40). Polyphonic synthesizer doubles the bass melody (Teen Town)

content: Short motifs like folk tunes that one can sing. Few notes.
parameters: Even eighth and sixteenth notes; little syncopation; short bursts in double time; no blues phrases. Solo of 42 bars at 120 BPM (2 x 16 + 10; computed 84 s); peak in bars 37-38. Notes: 67% modal, 22.8% tonal, 10.1% chromatic

content: A complex unison melody for the saxophones against a rhythm in 7/4 and a piano part that goes the other way.
parameters: 10:55 (1965). Later played at very fast tempos. Lines divided between the sections (hocket)

content: Guitar, bass, and keyboard play fast lines together.
parameters: The Romantic Warrior (10:52, acoustic): outro with fast unison patterns. The Magician (5:29): rapid unison lines. The Minimoog doubles the guitar line at 0:18 of the 11:26 track

content: Short horn figures and unison lines outside the key of the groove.
parameters: Trumpet figures of three notes with a trombone countermelody (Ostinato, at 1:30). Unison horn lines out of key (Hidden Shadows). Chant-like theme for trumpet and trombone (Hornets). Minimal horn riff on the blues scale (Chameleon)

item: Bass as chord and melody instrument
content: Two bass parts at once: chord arpeggios in the centre and heavy filtered notes at the sides. A falsetto voice above.
parameters: Seventh-chord arpeggios (centre); auto-wah notes (sides); voice from light tenor to chorused falsetto

content: A short, fast piece for bass, piano and programmed drums.
parameters: 2:16; 158 BPM (machine-detected); bass: Stephen Bruner; piano: Dennis Hamm; programming: Zack Sekoff

content: Jazz phrasing on the bass guitar against fully quantised drums. He often plays a harmonious bass part and writes electronic parts that fight it.
parameters: "nimble, melodic fretless bass"

item: Register and rhythm of the lead
content: The lead sits above the sub, the kick and the snare. It is not wide in stereo. Its rhythm copies or answers the hi-hat riff.
parameters: 200 to 800 Hz

item: Bass riff as the lead voice
content: Distorted mid-range bass riffs take the place of the sub as the main part. They work in the register of the electric guitar in heavy metal.
parameters: "robotic fluctuations and metal-esque aggression"

content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). Share of the intervals inside phrases. Repetition 4.6%; semitone 27.6%; whole tone 28.5%; 3 to 4 semitones 26.5%; 5 to 7 semitones 10.0%; 8 to 11 semitones 2.3%; octave and more 0.5%. Postbop and fusion: 4.8, 26.7, 28.8, 26.0, 10.9, 2.2, 0.6.
parameters: Steps 56%; thirds 26.5%; fourths and fifths 10%; larger 3%; repeats 5%

content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). Notes less than 134 ms apart: repetition 2.0%; semitone 33.8%; whole tone 29.8%; 3 to 4 semitones 24.9%; 5 to 7 semitones 7.9%; larger 1.6%. In bebop the semitone share is 40.9%.
parameters: Fast lines: steps 64%; thirds 25%; fourths and fifths 8%; chromatic share 34% (bebop 41%)

content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). Up 45.6%; down 49.8%; repetition 4.6%. A run in one direction has a mean of 2.13 intervals. 51.2% of the runs have one interval only. 15.3% have four or more. 5.0% have six or more.
parameters: Down : up = 1.09; direction change after 1 interval in 51% of the runs; long runs (6+) 5%

item: Interval classes in fast lines of two trumpeters
content: Hubbard's lines: steps 74.4% (down 46.5, up 27.9); 3 to 4 semitones 18.4%; 5 to 7 semitones 4.3%; larger 1.4%; repetition 1.5%. Shaw's lines: 63.0%; 22.7%; 12.7%; 0.4%; 1.2%. Fourths: Shaw 6.0% and 3.6% (the two directions), Hubbard 1.5% and 1.2%.
parameters: Scalar player: steps 74%; intervallic player: steps 63%, fourths and fifths 13%
where: Lines in 8 solos by each player

content: Mean absolute interval 2.66 semitones; SD of the intervals 3.33. Pitch range in a chorus 23.5 semitones. Rising to falling ratio 0.93. Tone repetitions 5.3%; large jumps up 2.2%. Chromatic runs have 3.2 tones; arpeggio runs 2.6 up and 2.5 down; falling step runs 3.9.
parameters: Chromatic run 3 tones; arpeggio run 2.5 tones; step run 4 tones; range 2 octaves per chorus
where: 1,416 choruses; values for 'all other' solos in the comparison tables

content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). Notes in a phrase: median 13; quartiles 8 and 24; 90th percentile 38. Duration: median 2.68 s; quartiles 1.49 and 4.40 s; 90th percentile 6.46 s. Brecker and Potter: median 18 notes (quartiles 9 and 35; 90th percentile 55); 3.03 s.
parameters: Phrase 8 to 24 notes, 1.5 to 4.4 s; virtuoso 9 to 35 notes, up to 55

artist: West Coast and East Coast players
item: Median tones in a phrase by player
content: Desmond 12; Sims 13; Getz 14; Baker 14.5; Mulligan 18; Konitz 24; Marsh 24. The ranges go from 1 to 79 tones.
parameters: Lyrical players 12 to 14 tones; line players 24 tones
where: Solos in the Weimar Jazz Database

content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). Rest after a phrase: median 0.67 s; quartiles 0.44 and 1.04 s; 90th percentile 1.56 s. In beats: median 1.88; quartiles 1.18 and 3.02. The soloist plays 80% of the time. Solos with funk feel: 75%; 90th percentile of the rest 2.56 s.
parameters: Rest 0.4 to 1.0 s (1.2 to 3 beats); play 75 to 82% of the time

content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). 34.3% of the phrases start on a beat and 65.7% between beats. First beat of the phrase: beat 1 31.7%; beat 2 24.6%; beat 3 24.7%; beat 4 18.8%. 38.3% of the phrases end on a beat.
parameters: Start off the beat in 2 of 3 phrases; no strong preference for beat 1

content: 140 solos have 4,939 units: a median of 32 for each solo and 13.75 for each chorus. Mean duration 2.25 s (SD 1.57). Licks are 45.7% of the units and lines 31.5%. Licks fill about 37% of the solo time and lines about 40%.
parameters: Unit 2.25 s; lick 0.46; line 0.32; other types 0.22
where: 140 solos (abstract read); time shares from the Jazzomat book

item: Chord tones on and off the beat
content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). A chord tone is the root, third, fifth or seventh of the written chord. On-beat notes: 52.1% chord tones. Off-beat notes: 48.1%. Last note of a phrase: 62.2%. Bebop: 53.7, 48.7, 65.0. Postbop and fusion: 48.0, 45.6, 55.9. 31.9% of the notes are on a beat.
parameters: Chord tone on beat 0.52; off beat 0.48; phrase end 0.62 (postbop: 0.48, 0.46, 0.56)
where: 193,018 notes; simple chord parser of this study

item: Pitch classes above the chord root
content: Measured in this task with a script on the open data file (not a published figure). Share of the notes by semitones above the root, all chords together: 0: 13.8; 1: 4.4; 2: 9.9; 3: 8.2; 4: 8.6; 5: 9.0; 6: 4.8; 7: 13.6; 8: 4.7; 9: 8.3; 10: 9.1; 11: 5.6 (percent).
parameters: Root and fifth 14% each; ninth 10%; fourth 9%; flat ninth, tritone, flat sixth 4 to 5% each

item: Share of notes outside the chord scale
content: Desmond 14.1% and Baker 18.2% non-diatonic tones. Hawkins and Byas: more than 20%. One Branford Marsalis solo: 20 to 30% in most choruses and almost 50% in the most outside chorus. Corpus shares of all tones: flat ninth 3.9%, tritone 4.2%.
parameters: Inside players 14 to 18%; postbop 20 to 30%; outside chorus up to 50%
where: Case studies in the Jazzomat book

item: The start of a phrase is simpler than the rest
content: The beginning of an improvised phrase has more frequent interval patterns, smaller intervals, less interval variety, less pitch variety and fewer direction changes.
parameters: Start a phrase with a common pattern and small intervals; make it more complex later

content: In 67 of 77 solos the on-beat eighth is louder than the off-beat eighth; in 10 solos the off-beat eighth is louder. The loudness falls over the phrase in 41 to 58% of the phrases. For many players higher notes are louder (r up to 0.55).
parameters: Accent the on-beat eighth by default; decrescendo over the phrase; higher = louder
where: Solos with at least 10 eighth-note pairs; loudness from separated audio

item: Swing ratio of a postbop tenor by tempo
content: 'I Mean You' (180 BPM): mean ratio 1.77:1, median 1.92:1. 'Midnight Voyage' (126 BPM): 1.7:1. 'Naked Soul' (92.4 BPM): 1.8:1. 'Peep' (320 BPM) and 'Cabin Fever' (300 BPM): rather straight eighths.
parameters: 1.7 to 1.9 at 90 to 180 BPM; about 1.0 at 300 BPM and more
where: Brecker solos in the Weimar Jazz Database
